What does it cost to install carpet in Snoqualmie, WA?

Plan on $4 to $7 per square foot installed in Snoqualmie, which covers the carpet, pad, labor, new tack strip and haul-away. Most projects total $2,000 to $4,500, while a 1,200 sq ft upper floor plus a staircase — the classic Ridge layout — usually comes in at $5,500 to $8,500. Carpet grade is the biggest variable, and you set it yourself with the samples on your own floor.
Will the mobile carpet showroom drive out to Snoqualmie?

It will. The van carries 20+ carpet samples and all three pad grades up Snoqualmie Parkway or into downtown, and we set the samples down in the exact rooms being carpeted so the color reads in your light, not a store's. Then every room and stair gets measured and your price gets written before we leave. The visit costs nothing.
What does carpet stretching cost in Snoqualmie?

Stretching starts at $99 per room in Snoqualmie. A power stretcher pulls ripples, waves and bunching back out for roughly a fifth of what new carpet would run, which makes it the smart move as long as the pile still stands up and you still like the color.
How much are carpeted stairs in a Snoqualmie home?

Stair carpet starts at $18 per step, installed waterfall or cap-and-band — your choice at the measure. Ridge two-stories often add a landing or a pie-shaped turn partway up, and those are counted into the written quote from the beginning instead of showing up later as an extra.
How long will my carpet installation take?

One day, for most Snoqualmie houses. A typical Ridge upstairs — three or four bedrooms plus the staircase — is a normal day's work for our crew. A packed full-house job with heavy furniture can roll into a second day, and the schedule is spelled out on your quote.
Do you move the furniture, or do I?

We do. Beds, dressers, couches and tables are included on most jobs, and everything goes back where it started. We only ask that you clear the small things first — closet floors, electronics, breakables, and anything you'd rather move with your own hands.
Should I restretch the carpet I have or replace it?

Stretch when the pile still stands, the backing is sound and the color still suits the room — that's a $99-per-room repair instead of a whole project. Replace when walk paths are crushed flat, seams are letting go, the backing is coming apart, or a pet smell has outlived professional cleaning. We tell you which side you're on before writing any quote.
What areas in and around Snoqualmie do you serve?

Everywhere in Snoqualmie — Snoqualmie Ridge, the historic downtown blocks off Railroad Ave, Kimball Creek and Meadowbrook — plus the Valley towns around us: North Bend, Fall City, Preston, Carnation and Snoqualmie Pass. Issaquah, Sammamish and the rest of the Eastside are an easy run for the van too.
Which carpet holds up best with dogs and cats?

Solution-dyed nylon over a moisture-barrier pad, with a sealed backing. The barrier keeps accidents from soaking into the subfloor — a soaked subfloor is what makes odor permanent — and solution-dyed fiber keeps its color even under diluted-bleach cleaning. The barrier pad upgrade starts at $0.65 per square foot, and the pet-ready samples are in the van on every Snoqualmie visit.
What warranty comes with the installation?

Every install carries OC Flooring's 1-year workmanship warranty, and the carpet carries its own mill warranty — usually 10 to 25 years on wear and stain depending on grade. Both appear on your written quote. Worth knowing: some mills tie their coverage to the pad underneath, which is exactly why all three pad grades come along to the visit.
